samf-senior-2007-r2-01.title: Count the two-minute periods
samf-senior-2007-r2-01.body:
A day has $24\times60=1440$ minutes, which is $720$ periods of two minutes. $\frac{8000}{720}\approx11$.

**Answer: (D) 11**

samf-senior-2007-r2-01.title: Step down by units
samf-senior-2007-r2-01.body:
$\frac{8000}{24}\approx333$ per hour, so $\frac{333}{30}\approx11$ per two minutes (there are $30$ two-minute periods in an hour).

**Answer: (D) 11**

samf-senior-2007-r2-03.title: Equal ratios
samf-senior-2007-r2-03.body:
Let the length be $L$ and the width $W$ ($L>W$). Folding along the shorter midline halves the length, giving a rectangle with sides $W$ and $\frac L2$. For similarity $\frac LW=\frac W{L/2}=\frac{2W}L$, so $L^2=2W^2$ and $\frac LW=\sqrt2$.

**Answer: (A) $\sqrt2$**

samf-senior-2007-r2-03.title: Paper sizes
samf-senior-2007-r2-03.body:
This is the property of A4 paper: halving a sheet gives a sheet of the same shape. If the shape has width $1$ and length $r$, then the half has width $\frac r2$ and length $1$, so $\frac r1=\frac1{r/2}$ gives $r^2=2$, $r=\sqrt2$ (indeed $A4\approx297:210\approx1.414$).

**Answer: (A) $\sqrt2$**

samf-senior-2007-r2-04.title: Circumference
samf-senior-2007-r2-04.body:
The circumference is $80\pi\approx251$ cm $\approx2.5$ m. In $120\,000$ m the wheel turns about $\frac{120\,000}{2.5}=48\,000$ times, so the nearest option is $50\,000$.

**Answer: (B) 50 000**

samf-senior-2007-r2-04.title: Rough estimate
samf-senior-2007-r2-04.body:
One rotation covers about $\pi\times0.8\approx2.5$ m, so $1$ km takes $\approx400$ rotations. For $120$ km that is $\approx48\,000$.

**Answer: (B) 50 000**

samf-senior-2007-r2-05.title: Perfect squares and cubes
samf-senior-2007-r2-05.body:
$a^3=b^2$ forces $a$ to be a perfect square and $b$ a perfect cube: write $a=k^2$, then $b=a^{3/2}=k^3$. We need $k^3\le100$, so $k=1,2,3,4$, giving $b=1,8,27,64$. Hence $4$ values.

**Answer: (D) 4**

samf-senior-2007-r2-05.title: Exponent argument
samf-senior-2007-r2-05.body:
Since $b^2$ is a perfect cube, in the prime factorisation of $b$ every exponent $e$ has $2e\equiv0\pmod3$, so $e$ is a multiple of $3$ and $b$ is a perfect cube. The cubes up to $100$ are $1,8,27,64$, and each works ($a=1,4,9,16$).

**Answer: (D) 4**

samf-senior-2007-r2-06.title: Similar triangles
samf-senior-2007-r2-06.body:
Triangles $PAB$ and $PDC$ are similar (as $AB\parallel CD$) with ratio $AB:CD=4:12=1:3$. Their heights from $P$ to the parallel lines are in the same ratio and add up to $8$, so they are $2$ and $6$. The distance from $P$ to $CD$ is $6$.

**Answer: (D) 6**

samf-senior-2007-r2-06.title: Coordinates
samf-senior-2007-r2-06.body:
Let $C=(0,0)$, $D=(12,0)$, $A=(a,8)$, $B=(a+4,8)$. A point on $BC$ is $P=t(a+4,8)$. A point on $AD$ is $P=(a+u(12-a),\,8-8u)$. Comparing $y$-coordinates gives $t=1-u$; comparing $x$-coordinates then gives $t(a+4)=a+(1-t)(12-a)$, which simplifies to $4t=12-12t$, so $t=\frac34$ (independent of $a$). So $P$ has height $8t=6$ above $CD$.

**Answer: (D) 6**

samf-senior-2007-r2-07.title: Compare powers
samf-senior-2007-r2-07.body:
$x<\frac58\iff3^x<3^{5/8}\iff2<3^{5/8}\iff2^8<3^5\iff256<243$, which is false. The other statements all check out in the same way: $x<\frac34\iff16<27$; $x>\frac47\iff2^7>3^4\iff128>81$; $x<\frac23\iff8<9$; $x>\frac35\iff2^5>3^3\iff32>27$.

**Answer: (D)**

samf-senior-2007-r2-07.title: Numerical value
samf-senior-2007-r2-07.body:
$x=\frac{\log2}{\log3}\approx0.6309$. Then $\frac34=0.75$, $\frac47\approx0.571$, $\frac23\approx0.667$, $\frac58=0.625$ and $\frac35=0.6$. Since $0.6309>0.625$, the statement $x<\frac58$ is false; the others are true.

**Answer: (D)**

samf-senior-2007-r2-08.title: Set up inequalities
samf-senior-2007-r2-08.body:
Let the fraction be $\frac x{x+16}$. Then $\frac59<\frac x{x+16}$ gives $5x+80<9x$, so $x>20$, and $\frac x{x+16}<\frac47$ gives $7x<4x+64$, so $x<21\frac13$. The only integer is $x=21$.

**Answer: (E) 21**

samf-senior-2007-r2-09.title: Inclusion-exclusion
samf-senior-2007-r2-09.body:
$500-40=460$ voters are in favour of at least one issue. If $x$ are in favour of both, then $375+275-x=460$, so $x=190$.

**Answer: (B) 190**

samf-senior-2007-r2-09.title: Venn diagram
samf-senior-2007-r2-09.body:
Only the first issue: $375-x$; only the second: $275-x$; both: $x$; neither: $40$. The total is $375-x+275-x+x+40=690-x=500$, so $x=190$.

**Answer: (B) 190**

samf-senior-2007-r2-10.title: Count pairs $(x,y)$
samf-senior-2007-r2-10.body:
For each of the $49$ pairs $(x,y)$ we need $z=12-x-y$ to be in $\{1,\dots,7\}$, i.e. $5\le x+y\le11$. The pairs with $x+y\le4$ are $1+2+3=6$ (sums $2,3,4$ occur $1,2,3$ ways), and the pairs with $x+y\ge12$ are $3+2+1=6$ (sums $12,13,14$ occur $3,2,1$ ways). So there are $49-6-6=37$ solutions.

**Answer: (A) 37**

samf-senior-2007-r2-10.title: Shift the variables
samf-senior-2007-r2-10.body:
Put $x=1+x'$ etc. with $0\le x',y',z'\le6$ and $x'+y'+z'=9$. Without upper bounds there are $\binom{11}2=55$ solutions; subtract those with a variable $\ge7$: for $x'\ge7$, let $x''=x'-7$ and $x''+y'+z'=2$, giving $\binom42=6$ solutions, and similarly for $y'$ and $z'$ ($18$ in all; two variables $\ge7$ is impossible). $55-18=37$.

**Answer: (A) 37**

samf-senior-2007-r2-11.title: Factorise
samf-senior-2007-r2-11.body:
Clearing fractions: $ab=6(a+b)$, so $(a-6)(b-6)=36$. With $a\le b$ and $a>6$ (since $\frac1a<\frac16$), the factorisations $36=1\cdot36,2\cdot18,3\cdot12,4\cdot9,6\cdot6$ give $(a,b)=(7,42),(8,24),(9,18),(10,15),(12,12)$. That is $5$ pairs.

**Answer: (E) 5**

samf-senior-2007-r2-11.title: Check by listing $a$
samf-senior-2007-r2-11.body:
Since $\frac1a<\frac16$ and $\frac1a\ge\frac1{12}$ (as $\frac1a\ge\frac1b$ means $\frac1a\ge\frac1{12}$), $7\le a\le12$. Then $\frac1b=\frac16-\frac1a=\frac{a-6}{6a}$, which is a unit fraction only for $a=7,8,9,10,12$ (giving $b=42,24,18,15,12$) and not for $a=11$ ($b=\frac{66}5$).

**Answer: (E) 5**

samf-senior-2007-r2-12.title: Remove the river
samf-senior-2007-r2-12.body:
The bridge has length $1$ wherever it is built. Close up the river so $M=N$; the shortest route $A$ to $B$ is then a straight line, the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $2+3=5$ and $12$, so it has length $13$. Reinserting the river adds the bridge of length $1$ without changing the rest, so the shortest path is $13+1=14$.

**Answer: (E) 14**

samf-senior-2007-r2-12.title: Check by a general position
samf-senior-2007-r2-12.body:
If the bridge is at horizontal position $t$ from $A$, the path length is $\sqrt{t^2+2^2}+1+\sqrt{(12-t)^2+3^2}$. By the triangle inequality the sum of the two square roots is at least $\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13$, with equality when $\frac t2=\frac{12-t}3$, i.e. $t=4.8$. So the minimum is $14$.

**Answer: (E) 14**

samf-senior-2007-r2-13.title: Compare coefficients
samf-senior-2007-r2-13.body:
Expanding $(x-a)(x-b)(x-c)=x^3-(a+b+c)x^2+(ab+bc+ca)x-abc$ and comparing: $a+b+c=a$, $ab+bc+ca=b$, $abc=c$. As $a,b,c\neq0$: $b+c=0$, $ab=1$, and $ab+bc+ca=b$. With $c=-b$ and $a=\frac1b$: $1-b^2-1=b$, so $b=-1$ (as $b\ne0$), $c=1$, $a=-1$. Then $p(2)=(2+1)(2+1)(2-1)=9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

samf-senior-2007-r2-14.title: Coordinates
samf-senior-2007-r2-14.body:
Let the square have side $3$: $A=(0,0)$, $B=(3,0)$, $C=(3,3)$, $D=(0,3)$ and $E=(1,0)$, $F=(3,1)$, $G=(2,3)$, $H=(0,2)$. The lines $AG$ and $EC$ both have direction $(2,3)$ and are a distance $\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}$ apart; the lines $HB$ and $DF$ both have direction $(3,-2)$ and are also $\frac3{\sqrt{13}}$ apart. They are perpendicular, so the shaded region is a square of area $\frac9{13}$. The whole square has area $9$, so shaded : whole $=1:13$ and the area of $ABCD$ is $13$.

**Answer: (C) 13**

samf-senior-2007-r2-14.title: Strips of equal width
samf-senior-2007-r2-14.body:
With side $3$, the parallelogram $AECG$ has base $AE=1$ and height $3$, so area $3$; it is also $AG\cdot w_1$ with $AG=\sqrt{13}$, so its width is $w_1=\frac3{\sqrt{13}}$. The parallelogram $HBFD$ has area $3$ too and $HB=\sqrt{13}$, so $w_2=\frac3{\sqrt{13}}$. The two perpendicular strips cross in the shaded square of side $\frac3{\sqrt{13}}$. Scaling so that this side is $1$ multiplies lengths by $\frac{\sqrt{13}}3$, so the side of $ABCD$ becomes $\sqrt{13}$ and its area $13$.

**Answer: (C) 13**

samf-senior-2007-r2-15.title: Day numbers
samf-senior-2007-r2-15.body:
April has $30$ days, so the $2k$-th day of May is the $(2k+30)$-th day of April. It is $(2k+30)-k=k+30$ days after the $k$-th day of April. We need $7\mid k+30$, so $k\equiv5\pmod7$: $k=5,12,19,26$. But $2k\le31$ requires $k\le15$, so only $k=5$ and $k=12$ work.

**Answer: (C) 2**

samf-senior-2007-r2-15.title: Check the end cases
samf-senior-2007-r2-15.body:
$k=5$: April 5 and May 10 are $35$ days apart. $k=12$: April 12 and May 24 are $42$ days apart. $k=19$ would need May 38, which does not exist. So there are $2$ values.

**Answer: (C) 2**

samf-senior-2007-r2-16.title: Divisibility by 3
samf-senior-2007-r2-16.body:
The total capacity is $119$ litres. The oil sold is divided in ratio $1:2$, so its volume is a multiple of $3$. We need $119-w$ divisible by $3$. Since $119\equiv2\pmod3$, we need $w\equiv2\pmod3$. Only $20$ qualifies ($15\equiv0$, $16\equiv1$, $18\equiv0$, $19\equiv1$, $20\equiv2$, $31\equiv1$). Check: $119-20=99=33+66$.

**Answer: (E) 20**

samf-senior-2007-r2-16.title: Test each barrel
samf-senior-2007-r2-16.body:
Removing $15,16,18,19,31$ leaves $104,103,101,100,88$, none divisible by $3$; removing $20$ leaves $99=3\cdot33$, which can be split $33:66$ (for example $15+18=33$ and $16+19+31=66$).

**Answer: (E) 20**

samf-senior-2007-r2-17.title: Frobenius coin problem
samf-senior-2007-r2-17.body:
For coprime $a,b$ the largest amount not representable as $ax+by$ with $x,y\ge0$ is $ab-a-b=42-13=29$.

**Answer: (A) 29**

samf-senior-2007-r2-17.title: Direct reasoning
samf-senior-2007-r2-17.body:
Using $k$ stamps of $7$ cents, amounts $7k+6m$ cover all numbers $\equiv7k\pmod6$ that are at least $7k$. With $k=0,\dots,5$ (residues $0,1,\dots,5$ mod $6$) the amounts $0,7,14,21,28,35$ each start a residue class; the last class to start is $35\equiv5$, so the largest gap is $35-6=29$.

**Answer: (A) 29**

samf-senior-2007-r2-18.title: Closed form
samf-senior-2007-r2-18.body:
From $f(x,y)=f(0,y)+x(y+1)$ and $f(0,y)=f(y,0)=y$ we get $f(x,y)=x+y+xy$. This is symmetric and satisfies all the conditions, so $f(12,5)=12+5+60=77$.

**Answer: (A) 77**

samf-senior-2007-r2-19.title: Arithmetic progression of angles
samf-senior-2007-r2-19.body:
Let the smallest angle be $a$ and the common difference $d\ge0$ (both integers). The angle sum gives $5a+10d=540$, so $a=108-2d$. The largest angle is $a+4d=108+2d$, which must be less than $180^\circ$ for convexity, so $d<36$. Also $a>0$ requires $d<54$. So $d=0,1,\dots,35$, each giving a different $a$, which is $36$ values.

**Answer: (D) 36**

samf-senior-2007-r2-19.title: Check the ends
samf-senior-2007-r2-19.body:
$d=0$: all angles $108^\circ$, smallest $108$. $d=35$: angles $38,73,108,143,178$ (all $<180$). $d=36$ would give $180^\circ$, not convex. So $36$ values of $a$: $108,106,\dots,38$.

**Answer: (D) 36**

samf-senior-2007-r2-20.title: Tangent lengths
samf-senior-2007-r2-20.body:
The right angle makes the hypotenuse a diameter of the big circle, so the hypotenuse is $D$. The small circle has radius $\frac d2$ and touches the legs; the tangent lengths from the right-angle vertex are $\frac d2$, so from the other vertices they are $a-\frac d2$ and $b-\frac d2$. The hypotenuse is the sum of these two: $D=a+b-d$, so $D+d=a+b$.

**Answer: (A) $a+b$**

samf-senior-2007-r2-20.title: Inradius formula
samf-senior-2007-r2-20.body:
For a right triangle, inradius $r=\frac{a+b-c}2$ with hypotenuse $c=D$. Then $d=2r=a+b-D$, so $D+d=a+b$. Check with $a=3,b=4,c=5$: $r=1$, $d=2$, $D+d=7=a+b$.

**Answer: (A) $a+b$**
